Agenda Materials
The complete agenda packet is available at cerritos.gov and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st Floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours as posted. Materials received after posting of the agenda will also be available for public inspection. For assistance, contact the Office of the City Clerk at city_clerk@cerritos.gov or (562) 916-1248.
Order of Agenda
The City Council may reorder agenda items by majority vote of members present.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public may observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at cerritos.gov/agendas or the City’s YouTube channel , on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public comment may be provided in person, remotely via Zoom, or in writing as described below. Public comment on business agenda items will be heard during consideration of that business item. Public comment on Consent Calendar, Closed Session, and non-agenda items will be heard during Agenda Item No. 6.

Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. Timely comments will be distributed to the legislative body and retained as part of the official record.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact City of Cerritos ADA/504 Coordinator, Drew Schneider, at (562) 916-1314 at least 72 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

  1. Account/Project:  110363-67020 (MWD Purchase)
  110363-65213 (Water Well Pumping)
  Amount:  $810,000
  Justification: A budget transfer of $810,000 is requested from the Water Well
  Pumping Assessment account to the MWD Purchase account to cover increased
  imported water costs for July 2026 through October 2026. The C-1 Well was
  initially taken out of service in March 2026 due to a mechanical gear head failure
  and, although repairs have been completed, the C-1 Well remains offline while
  the City addresses ongoing manganese-related water quality and regulatory
  matters with the California Division of Drinking Water. Because the C-1 Well is
  offline, water well pumping assessment expenditures related to this well will be
  lower than originally budgeted from July 2026 through October 2026. This results
  in $402,000 of available funds from the Water Well Pumping Assessment account
  to be transferred to the MWD Purchase account to assist in offsetting costs for
  the more expensive imported water.

  The C-4 Well was recently brought back online in June 2026 with reduced
  pumping capacity. The reduced capacity results in an estimated annual savings in
  FY 2026-2027 of $408,000 in the Water Well Pumping Assessment account to be
  transferred to the MWD Purchase account to offset costs for the more expensive
  imported water; and
